analysis.title: Weekly Fund Flows: Before the Wave
key_insights: Global equity funds took in +$89bn in the week ending November 4, up from +$56bn the prior week. The four-week sum is $265.5bn.
Developed market inflows were led by US and Japan funds. US equity funds took in $31.7bn on the week and Japan funds $3.8bn. Western Europe funds saw net outflows of $1.3bn.
Emerging market equity funds took in $45.1bn on the week, driven by continued domestic inflows to Mainland China funds ($34.5bn). Taiwan funds added $8.6bn.
Technology funds again saw the largest sector inflows ($15.9bn on the week, $71.5bn over four weeks) despite recent AI-driven equity volatility. Telecom funds saw the largest outflows (-$2.2bn).
The data do not capture the extent of market moves in the latter half of the week following the US midterm elections.

Fixed income funds took in $11.8bn on the week. Long-duration, short-duration and inflation-protected bond funds all saw inflows. EM fixed income saw -$6.0bn, with local-currency funds at -$5.6bn and hard-currency funds still in outflow.
Money market fund assets increased by $140bn on the week, against $3.4bn the prior week.
Cross-border FX flows were $22.1bn on the week and well-supported in G10 and Asia, driven by flows into USD ($9.9bn) and CNY ($2.3bn).
The pace of flows into USD has re-accelerated this year after a more subdued 2025.
risk_factors: AI-driven equity volatility, which the report says is not fully reflected in the flow data
Market moves after the US midterm elections in the latter half of the week are not captured in the flows
charts_described: Chart of the Week (Exhibit 1, cumulative cross-border fund flows 2022 to present for USA, Euro area and China) accompanies the text noting that the pace of flows into USD has re-accelerated this year after a more subdued 2025.
vol_and_positioning: Equity fund flows over the four weeks to November 4 have a z-score of 4.27 on the four-week sum, with EM at 4.32 and technology at 3.87.
Money market inflows of $140bn in one week ran at 1.24% of AUM, against a four-week average of 0.26%.
Utilities (z-score -2.80), consumer goods (-1.60) and industrials (-2.17) saw four-week outflows. High-beta funds saw -$3.4bn and low-beta funds -$7.1bn over four weeks.
geopolitical: US midterm elections took place during the week and moved markets in the latter half of it, after the flow data window closed
